newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CONTINUES FALL ON KEY U.S. UNIT.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CONTINUES FALL ON KEY U.S. UNIT.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar continued falling on the key U.S. dollar on Wednesday, pressured by a combination of mild importer demand and players quoting prices on the U.S. unit higher to protect meagre foreign currency reserves.
"We're seeing a technical slide in the Zimbabwe dollar. Most people are just quoting high to protect their positions and we've been losing a cent or two everyday since Monday," said one dealer.
"There's some import pressure filtering in but not in a very big way," another said.
Dealers said some importers were beginning to panic and seeking to pay off their creditors in advance, before the local unit depreciated further.
At around 0800 GMT the Zimbabwe dollar was trading at 11.0725/0825 against the U.S. unit from late Tuesday's 11.0700/0800.

On the crosses, it was quoted firmer against sterling at 17.8190/8460 compared to 17.8700/9100 the previous day but was weaker on the mark at 6.5800/5900 from 6.5000/5100. Against South Africa's rand it edged up marginally to 2.4600/4700 from 2.4700/4800.
